solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Breton speaker maybe caught in shower

indicators.note: one item sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word

blocks.note: a pelt is a heavy downpour
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Breton is caught out in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: A P-Celt speaks a Brythonic language such as Breton or Welsh, as opposed to a Q-Celt, who speaks Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is one of the Brythonic or P-Celtic tongues, so its speaker is one example of the group.

clue.text: Catholic (to detractors), head as of old full of sanctimonious stuff

indicators.note: a word full of something contains it, so the second piece goes inside

blocks.note: pash is an old word for the head, used by Shakespeare
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious talk

explanation.surface: A Catholic is mocked as an old head stuffed with piety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head as of old' warns that the word is archaic; Shakespeare uses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Papish is a hostile term for Roman Catholic, used by those who disparage popery.

clue.text: Evergreen climber displaying tangled caulis

indicators.note: tangled letters are knotted up out of order and must be straightened

blocks.note: taken as written; a caulis is a plant stem

explanation.surface: A climbing plant shows its tangled stems.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusia is a genus of tropical evergreen shrubs and trees, many of which climb or start life as epiphytes.

clue.text: One of many in the north to take a break from work there

definitions.text: One of many in the north
to take a break from work there

blocks.clueFragment: One of many in the north
blocks.note: first meaning: one of the many ... of the ... District in north-west England

blocks.clueFragment: to take a break from work there
blocks.note: second meaning: a northern dialect verb meaning to play or skive off work

explanation.surface: Northerners like to take a day off at one of their many waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' means in the north: lake (or laik) is northern English dialect for playing truant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District in Cumbria has many lakes, and northern dialect uses the same word for taking time off to play.

clue.text: Take advantage of pictures etc put up, done badly (7, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means its letters read bottom to top
badly done means botched, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: pictures and the like are art
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exploits paintings that were hung badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade on something is to exploit it for one's own benefit, as with a reputation.

clue.text: Strip of metal, line inside corrected backing

indicators.note: inside tells us the one letter is lodged within the longer word
backing means going in reverse, so the whole result is read from right to left

blocks.note: corrected work has been revised
L is the usual abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a line in a text and then reverses the change, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Put L inside REVISED to make REVLISED, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To desilver is to remove the silver coating or content from something, stripping it of that metal.

clue.text: It's havoc if station's lacking good spirit

indicators.note: lacking means without, so one word is taken out of the other

blocks.note: havoc is widespread devastation
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: It would be chaos if the station had no morale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of station's makes it read as possession, but it means station is.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief a deva is a god or benevolent divine being, a good spirit.

clue.text: Campaign worker broadcast lie etc, a whopper

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so these letters are dispersed and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
a one-er is something outstanding, a big one

explanation.surface: A campaigner spreads a lie, and a huge one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whopper' looks like a big lie in the surface, but here it is ONEER, a variant of oner, a remarkable thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An electioneer is someone who canvasses and campaigns to get a candidate elected.

clue.text: Lancashire's opener cracking six – a piece of cake?

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, the only one taken
cracking something open means getting inside it

blocks.note: sice is the six at dice
the first letter of Lancashire

explanation.surface: A Lancashire opening batsman hits a six: easy?
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface suggests 'a piece of cake' means easy, but it is a literal slice. Lancashire is an English county with a well-known cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice is a wedge cut from a cake, literally a piece of it.

clue.text: Party losing muscle? It's looking gloomy

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a lour is a gloomy look

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so letters are dropped from the party

blocks.note: the Labour Party, one of Britain's main parties
ab is short for an abdominal muscle

explanation.surface: A party has lost its strength and the outlook is bleak.
explanation.definitionFit: A lour is a scowl or a threatening, dark appearance, the look of something gloomy.

clue.text: Composition for a violoncello (quartet lost) or other instrument

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh
a quartet is four, so four letters, here the last four, are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the full word, before trimming its end

explanation.surface: A piece is written for cello, or for another instrument, without the string quartet.
explanation.walkthrough: The last four letters of violoncello, ELLO, are lost; A plus VIOLONC is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalion is a kind of reed organ resembling a harmonium, an instrument other than the cello.

clue.text: Invigorate partly low energy, given a lift

indicators.note: partly means only part of the following words is used
in a down clue, lifting the letters makes them read bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of low and the start of energy

explanation.surface: Someone with partly low energy is perked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore its freshness and vigour, to revitalise it.

clue.text: Drugs jar, overturned jar, left empty inside

indicators.note: something overturned is turned the other way round, so its letters are read backwards
inside says the following pieces are placed within the overturned word

blocks.note: an olla is an earthenware jar or pot
L is the abbreviation for left
an empty room is a bare one

explanation.surface: An apothecary's jar is tipped over and left with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The insert goes in after the first letter of the reversed jar, not dead centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An albarello is a maiolica pharmacy jar, traditionally used to hold dry drugs and ointments.

clue.text: Litter from end of picnicking in wood? It's mounting

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept
in places that letter inside the wood
in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: oak is a wood
the final letter of picnicking

explanation.surface: Rubbish left after a woodland picnic is piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish, but it is the old sense of a carried couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A kago is a Japanese palanquin, a litter carried on poles by bearers.

clue.text: Hard disc in sport area, durable

blocks.note: the puck is the hard rubber disc used in ice hockey
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: The rubber disc used in a game is said to be hard-wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: PUCKA is a variant spelling of pukka, from Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: Pucka or pukka means genuine and solidly made, hence lasting and substantial.

clue.text: Evangelist's contribution to vernacular making comeback

indicators.note: a contribution to something is only a part of it, so the letters come from inside the next word
coming back means returning the way it came, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A gospel writer's contribution to everyday speech is returning to fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters NACUL inside vernacular, read backwards, spell LUCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucan is the adjective for St Luke, so it means belonging to that evangelist, matching the possessive.

clue.text: A bishop on a bishop's seat, new installed in fine embroidery

indicators.note: something installed is placed within, so the letter goes inside the seat

blocks.note: taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
taken as written
a see is a bishop's seat or diocese
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A bishop sits on another bishop's throne amid a newly embroidered cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the first bishop comes before the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrasene is a woollen or silk embroidery thread, and needlework done with it.

clue.text: Cheer up once having kicked coca craze

indicators.note: kicked about, these letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a craze is the rage, the latest fashion

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered after quitting a cocaine habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the answer as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Accorage is an archaic verb meaning to encourage or hearten, the old sense of cheering someone up.

clue.text: Ancestor penning opening for troubadour's speciality

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a sire is a forefather
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A forebear wrote something that launched a minstrel's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like it means a first letter, but it is a whole word for an aperture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sirvente is a satirical or moralising song of the medieval Provençal troubadours, a form they made their own.

clue.text: Sandy's fastened most of metal tools

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

blocks.note: steel is a metal
a kit is a set of tools

explanation.surface: A Scotsman has fixed most of his metal toolkit.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy is the crossword's stock Scotsman, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Steekit is the Scots past participle of steek, meaning shut or fastened.

clue.text: Good base for healthy complexion

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
base in the sense of mean or contemptible

explanation.surface: A good foundation cream suits a healthy skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good base' reads as make-up, but base means low.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is the warm flush of colour in the cheeks of a healthy person.

clue.text: A third Marconi distorted in common chord (13, two words)

indicators.note: something distorted is twisted out of shape, so these letters lose their original order

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A third of a Marconi radio signal is garbled in an ordinary chord.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'third' is musical, which helps disguise that these words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonic triad is the root, third and fifth sounded together, which musicians also call the common chord.

clue.text: Sheep and a variety of hens

blocks.note: first meaning: a short-legged breed of sheep
second meaning: a breed of mottled domestic fowl

explanation.walkthrough: Both breeds take their name from the Italian port of Ancona.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ancona is a breed of mottled black-and-white poultry, and also an old breed of short-legged sheep.

clue.text: Maid holding large ungulate? Employ one for striking character (6, two words)

indicators.note: holding means clasping something within, so the animal goes inside

blocks.note: a dey is an old word for a dairymaid
the elk is a large deer, a hoofed mammal

explanation.surface: A milkmaid hangs on to a big hoofed animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests hitting, but it means striking out; the delete key on a keyboard erases a character.
explanation.definitionFit: The delete key is pressed to erase a typed character, so it is what you use to strike one out.

clue.text: Mop was in a mess – head for barber

indicators.note: a word in a mess has its letters jumbled out of order
the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of barber

explanation.surface: A mop of hair was untidy, so off to the barber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mop' suggests hair, given the barber, but it is the cleaning tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop for cleaning decks or floors, and to swab is to mop.

clue.text: Morag's nimble woman in loose gown

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the gown

blocks.note: a sack or sacque is a loose-fitting gown
W is the abbreviation for woman

explanation.surface: A Scotswoman moves nimbly in a loose dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Morag, a Scottish name, marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swack is a Scots adjective for lithe, supple and agile, which is what nimble means.

clue.text: Last to show age will folk shrivel, being old?

indicators.note: the last of each word is its final letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the final letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Will people wither when they finally start to look old?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being old' tells us the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Welk is an obsolete verb meaning to wither or fade, as old people and plants shrivel.

clue.text: It'll kill fish, joint being thrust into mass of their eggs

indicators.note: thrusting one thing into another places it inside that other word

blocks.note: roe is a mass of fish eggs
a tenon is the projecting part of a mortise-and-tenon joint

explanation.surface: A joint stuck into a fish's roe will be the end of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests cannabis in the surface, but it is the woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotenone is a plant-derived insecticide that is highly toxic to fish and is used to clear ponds of them.

clue.text: Satellite channel exercised having lost director twice

indicators.note: having lost means without, so letters are removed

blocks.note: soldiers exercised on parade are drilled
D for director, taken twice

explanation.surface: A TV channel lost two directors after working them hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite channel' looks like television; the satellite is the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rille is a long narrow trench or valley on the Moon's surface, the Moon being Earth's satellite.

clue.text: Heading for the sunsets from Scotland, news breaking about list at sea

definitions.text: Heading for the sunsets from Scotland

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second
news breaking is shattered into pieces, so the combined letters are rearranged
something at sea is confused and adrift, reinforcing that the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailing west from Scotland, news arrives about a ship listing in heavy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' looks like a noun for a headline, fitting the news, but it means travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Westlins is a Scots adverb meaning westward, the direction in which the sun sets.

clue.text: No longer showing restraint, in part of Dirty Den

indicators.note: in part of means the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: the end of Dirty and start of Den

explanation.surface: Dirty Den, the soap villain, has lost all self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirty Den was a notorious character in the British TV soap EastEnders. Tyde is a Spenserian form of tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied means held in restraint; 'no longer' marks tyde as an obsolete spelling.

clue.text: Scotch fatty downed rapidly

blocks.note: first meaning: a Scots word for a fat person
second meaning: gone down quickly, as a ship does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed rapidly' suggests gulping a drink, a fitting partner for Scotch whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunk is the past participle of sink, to go down fast; Scots also uses sunk for a stout person.

clue.text: Stop around middle of psalms for Gloria

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the selected letters
the middle of a word is its central letters, the only ones kept

blocks.note: ho is an old call to stop
the two central letters of psalms

explanation.surface: A pause in the middle of the psalms for the Gloria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloria' looks like the hymn, but in art a gloria is a halo or aureole.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloria is a halo of light painted round a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Calm earlier, one's heading for large centre of cyclone

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is all that is taken

blocks.note: A means one, as in a single thing
the opening letter of large
the eye is the calm centre of a cyclone

explanation.surface: Before the storm the air is calm, a sign of a big cyclone approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' marks an old spelling: aleye is an obsolete form of allay.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay is to soothe or quieten, and aleye is that verb's earlier spelling.

clue.text: Stuffing, one tucked into nuts, right?

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: KP is a well-known British brand of salted nuts
A means one
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it's all right to put a filling into nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: KP nuts are a familiar packet snack in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapok is the silky fibre from a tropical tree, used as stuffing for cushions and life jackets.

clue.text: Nile up-lane diverted, not a regular monthly phenomenon

indicators.note: something diverted is sent off its course, so the letters are rearranged
not here means without, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: every letter of these words
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Traffic is rerouted from a Nile road, not something that happens every month.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'not a regular monthly phenomenon' as one phrase, but 'not a' is the deletion and the definition follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenilune is a poetic word for the full moon, which recurs about once a month.

clue.text: King's fool (annoying) about to move faster backwards – it's automatic

indicators.note: backwards means the word is written from its end to its start
about means around, so the fool goes round the reversed word

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
nerk is British slang for an irritating fool
jee is a variant of gee, as in gee up, to urge on faster

explanation.surface: A king's jester, an irritating one, is about to scuttle off backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to', but about is the container signal and 'to move faster' is the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk reaction is a reflex made without thinking, like the doctor's hammer test on the knee.

clue.text: Lizard that's all right replacing most of tail

indicators.note: replacing means one string of letters takes the place of another

blocks.note: okay means all right
all but the first letter of tail, its last three, is swapped out, leaving its T

explanation.surface: A lizard that has shed most of its tail is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Lizards can regrow lost tails, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The tokay is a large gecko of South-East Asia, named for its loud call.
